original_question: Suppose a graph G satisfies |E(H)| <= c|V(H)|^2 for every subgraph H of G. Does it follow that lambda(G) <= 2c|V(G)|? More generally, what bound should replace this when the exponent 2 is replaced by another constant less than 2?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 1 (Guiduli): the open problem asking whether the hereditary density condition |E(H)| <= c|V(H)|^2 for every subgraph H of G forces the adjacency spectral radius bound lambda(G) <= 2c|V(G)|, and asking what bound should replace this when the exponent 2 is replaced by a constant less than 2.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual formulation. It correctly identifies the hereditary hypothesis on every subgraph H of G, the target bound lambda(G) <= 2c|V(G)|, and the paper's explicit follow-up asking what happens when the exponent 2 is replaced by another constant less than 2.
missing_details: The paper works throughout with finite simple, undirected, unweighted graphs.
lambda(G) means the largest adjacency eigenvalue lambda_1(G), i.e. the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix A(G).
The quantifier is over every subgraph H of G; the paper does not restrict to induced subgraphs.
The question is posed as a nonlinear generalization of the preceding Hereditarily Bounded Property P_{t,r}, where |E(H)| <= t|V(H)| + r for all subgraphs H with |V(H)| >= t.

The nearby discussion records the weaker trivial estimate lambda(G) <= sqrt(2c)|V(G)| from lambda(G) <= sqrt(2|E(G)|), and explains that the coefficient 2c would be best possible if the stated bound were true, by comparison with Wilf's inequality.
The second sentence is intentionally qualitative in the paper: it does not propose a specific replacement bound, only asks what can be said when the exponent is any fixed constant less than 2.
refined_question: Let G be a finite simple undirected unweighted graph, and let lambda(G)=lambda_1(G) denote the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix. Suppose there exists a constant c such that every subgraph H \subseteq G satisfies |E(H)| <= c|V(H)|^2. Must it follow that lambda(G) <= 2c|V(G)|? More generally, if every subgraph H \subseteq G satisfies |E(H)| <= c|V(H)|^alpha for some fixed constant alpha<2, what upper bound on lambda(G) in terms of c, alpha, and |V(G)| should replace 2c|V(G)|?
justification: The draft is targeting Guiduli's Problem 1 in Section 4 almost verbatim. The immediately preceding theorem and definition show that this problem is framed as a generalization of Guiduli's linear hereditary edge-bound property P_{t,r}, so that context should be retained but not broadened. To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, the main additions needed are the paper's standing graph conventions and the definition of lambda(G) as the top adjacency eigenvalue. I have therefore kept the scope exactly at the paper's open problem, without replacing it by a broader extremal-spectral question.
